one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled events fall in the window. September sales come out Oct 8 (TSMC calendar). July+August revenue was NT$982B, so even a September at or below August beats the US$44.6-45.8B 3Q guide; that beat is expected. 3Q26 results and 4Q guidance come Oct 15, where the swing factors are 4Q GM (N2 and overseas-fab dilution) and early 2027 capex commentary. The sell side now expects $85-90B for 2027 (UBS $90B, BofA $85B), so a big capex number is partly expected. After the July beat-and-raise the ADR fell. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28: Kalshi has about 66% hold / 34% hike (Oct 2), down from 65% hike odds on Sep 25. The 10-year touched its highest level since 2002 on Oct 1 (~5.3%) before easing to 5.24%. Momentum is positive (near the 52-week high, +10% since August), but TSM's reactions to earnings have been mixed and rates are a live headwind. Net: I center on about $461 (+0.4%) with monthly vol of about 11.2% (40%/3.5) and a 3% fat-tail component for an earnings or rates shock. That is slightly less bullish than round 1 (P>=spot 0.514 vs 0.529).

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 19x forward P/E on Oct-2027 NTM EPS of about $24.4/ADR (0.25 x CY27 consensus $21.93 + 0.75 x CY28 estimate $25.2), giving $464, weight 0.6; and (b) the 10-year median trailing P/E of 20.5x (replacing the 22x average, which was inflated by the 2019-21 zero-rate years) on CY27 EPS of $21.93, giving $450, weight 0.4. The blend is about $458. Both multiples are cut for a 10-year yield of ~5.25-5.3%, the highest since 2002.

10-year median ~20.4x instead of the ~22.4x average. The average is pulled up by the 2019-21 and 2024-25 years of 27-32x, which mostly came with 10-year yields of 0.5-4.5%. With the 10-year now ~5.25-5.3%, the median is the better rate-neutral anchor. The long-run (1997-2026) median of ~15.9x sets a floor reference.

bear.story: AI capex digestion and/or a 2027 US recession (Kalshi ~24%, Polymarket ~35% by end-2027) hit a stock on a cycle-high multiple, while a 5%+ 10-year leaves no valuation cushion. The SOX median drawdown is -35%; TSM fell ~50% in 2022 (the last hiking cycle) and ~33% in 2024-25. That means ~15x on ~$20 EPS. A Taiwan shock (Polymarket 13% invasion by end-2027) is a fatter tail below this.

base.story: EPS compounds ~25-30% into 2027 (consensus revised up 9/0) as N2 ramps and CoWoS stays tight, but the multiple compresses from ~21x CY27 to ~19-19.5x NTM under 5%+ rates and an $85-90B capex step-up. The price grows only modestly, roughly with fair value plus a small revisions drift.

bull.story: The AI cycle extends like 2023-24 or 2015-18 (SOX +70% through a hiking cycle when a secular build-out ran). CY28 EPS moves toward $27-28 on price hikes and strong revenue, and the stock holds ~24-25x. A softer Fed path (Kalshi October hike odds already fell from 65% to 34%) eases the rate headwind.

thesis_break_reason: $330 is ~28% below spot, below the March 2026 low area ($314-338), ~15x the confirmed (and rising) $21.93 CY27 consensus and ~13.5x Oct-2027 NTM EPS: bottom-quartile valuation even on the 1997-2026 long-run median of ~16x. Getting there would most likely mean the market expects 2027 earnings to fall (hyperscaler AI capex cuts, a GM reset, a severe Section 232 widening or a Strait blockade scare), not ordinary 40%-vol noise. I keep it unchanged; the higher rate backdrop lowers fair value but does not make 15x forward a normal level for a business growing 25%+.

Thin conditional base rate: ~10 high-momentum episodes (about 6 independent cycles) with roughly coin-flip outcomes
reasoning: Round 2 changes three things. (1) Base rate. Following the supervisor, I re-ran TSM's monthly history on the full 1997-2026 series (325 overlapping 12-month windows). Unconditional 12-month log return: mean +16%, sd 36%. Conditioning on a trailing gain >45% gives 58 months, but they fall in only 10 clusters (1999-2000, 2002, 2003-04, 2009, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2020-21, 2024-25, 2025): roughly 6 independent cycles. Forward median +2%, 53% positive, cluster-median median ~0% (5 of 10 positive; excluding the dot-com bust ~+15%). Round 1's +21% median/62% positive came from a shorter window starting 2000-03 that dropped most of the 1999-2000 run-up, and it leaned on too few episodes. I no longer let the conditional rate set the median; it says only that momentum years end up roughly a coin flip with very wide outcomes. (2) Rates. The 10-year touched its highest level since 2002 on Oct 1 (~5.3%) and closed near 5.24-5.30%. The Fed hiked on Sep 16. My 22x trailing leg came from a low-rate decade, so I replaced it with the 10-year median (20.5x) and cut the forward multiple from 20x to 19x. History says not to over-do this: in hiking cycles the SOX did well when a secular build-out ran (1994, 1999, 2015-18) and badly in digestion phases (2004-06, 2022). The 2004-07 15-17x P/Es came with far lower growth. Fair value falls from $487 to $458. (3) Fundamentals checked by the supervisor: FY27 EPS $21.93 with 9/0 upward revisions (a mild positive drift), 2027 capex $85-90B (higher D&A, already broadly in estimates), and the VIS gain as a 2026 one-off. The thin AI-bubble Polymarket ($9k) is dropped as a driver. Ladder: 95% lognormal with median $478 (+4%: fair value ~$458-464 plus a revisions/momentum drift, below round 1's $492) and sigma 0.35, plus a 5% crash state with median $210 for Taiwan or a severe AI bust. P(>=spot) is 0.52 (round 1: 0.55), the mean is about $495, and the scenario mean is about $485. Two modest disagreements with the supervisor: I keep a 0.6/0.4 blend of two P/E legs (I did not model FCF, so the capex correction affects my numbers only through the EPS path), and my fair value of $458 sits a little below its $470 because I anchor the trailing leg on the 10-year median rather than a higher multiple. Research was limited to about 7 follow-up queries plus a recomputation; the CNBC and Kalshi pages were blocked (403/429), so those figures come from search summaries and secondary trackers. No option data used.
